gamelink-agent - expose approved game ports through Tailcat (no router port forwarding)

Usage:
  gamelink-agent [--dir DIR] <command> [options]

Setup:
  init                          create the agent configuration directory
  games add                     expose a game port (generates the game's own Tailcat identity)
  games list                    list configured games
  games remove <id>             stop exposing a game and delete its identity

Access control (per game; a game with no approved devices is unreachable):
  devices approve               approve a friend's public key for one game
  devices revoke                revoke a device (a running agent restarts that game and ends the session)
  devices list                  list approved devices

Sharing and running:
  invite                        print the invitation a friend imports into GameLink (a secret)
  serve                         run the agent in the foreground (Ctrl-C / SIGTERM to stop)
  status                        show games, approvals and whether the agent is running
  version                       print the version

The configuration directory defaults to $GAMELINK_AGENT_DIR, else
<user config dir>/gamelink-agent. Run 'gamelink-agent <command> -h' for options.

Usage of games add:
  -bedrock-ip string
    	Bedrock server LAN IPv4 address
  -bridge-bind-ip string
    	agent LAN IPv4 address
  -console-bridge
    	enable Bedrock LAN console bridge
  -description string
    	optional short description
  -dest string
    	where to forward to, as ip:port (default: 127.0.0.1:<port>); use this for Docker or Pterodactyl
  -id string
    	short identifier (default: derived from the name)
  -media-ports string
    	allowed Bedrock media port range, e.g. 19132-19136
  -name string
    	display name shown to friends (default: the game type's name)
  -port int
    	port inside the tunnel (default: the game's standard port)
  -proto string
    	tcp or udp (required for custom games)
  -relay-host string
    	use your own DERP relay at this host name instead of the public relays
  -relay-region int
    	use this region of the public Tailcat relay map (default: nearest)
  -type string
    	game type: minecraft-java, minecraft-bedrock, factorio or custom (required)

Usage of devices approve:
  -game string
    	game id (required)
  -key string
    	the friend's public key, nodekey:... (required)
  -label string
    	a name to remember this device by

Usage of devices revoke:
  -game string
    	game id (required)
  -key string
    	public key to revoke, nodekey:... (required)

Usage of devices list:
  -game string
    	only this game

Usage of invite:
  -allow-local-relay
    	allow a relay on a private IP (for LAN-only test setups)
  -game string
    	game id (required)
  -name string
    	name shown in the friend's GameLink (default: the game's name)
  -note string
    	optional short note shown on import

Usage of serve:
  -verbose
